_comment: Proof cells + reference netlists for the gf180mcu LVS bring-up (issue
#51), and what `klt extract` / `klt lvs` are each expected to say.
run_lvs.py runs the extraction once and both LVS cases listed here, and
FAILS the run if any reported field does not match `expect*` exactly --
that assertion is the whole point: it is what distinguishes a green
bring-up from an LVS pass that never actually compared anything.
extract       run live every invocation (not just --regen) to prove
`klt extract` itself, not only its cached output.
generator   script that (re)builds `gds`, run with an interpreter
that has the pip `klayout` package.
gds         committed GDSII stream, byte-reproducible (see
gen_lvs_unit.py), so `sha256` is a real integrity check.
netlist     committed SPICE netlist `klt extract` produces from `gds`
-- regenerated (not hand-edited) by run_lvs.py --regen,
and re-verified byte-for-byte against a fresh extraction
on every plain run (extraction is deterministic: no
wall-clock/random content -- verified while implementing
this bring-up). This is the file both lvs_request_*.json
below point their `layout.netlist` at.
expect      the exact `klt extract --deck <deck> --format json`
fields the extraction must reproduce (dbu_um,
device_count, net_count, pin_count, device_counts,
devices, nets). `devices[].nets`/`params` and `nets[]`
are the load-bearing part: they are what proves the
Metal1 (34/10) pin labels actually named the nets, not
just that *some* netlist came out.
expect.device_classes
the deck's own declared device-class list, echoed by
`klt extract --format json`. Pinned here (issue #70)
because ../../toolchain.json's capability probe can
only see `klt`'s VERBS, and this repo now depends on
the gf180mcu DECK recognising
`cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield`. A `klt` from before that
landed has every required verb and would pass the pin
check while silently extracting the CDAC unit
capacitor as ordinary interconnect.
expect.warnings (block_extractions only)
one substring per warning `klt extract` is expected
to emit, in order; the count must match exactly. Two
are real, permanent and pinned rather than silenced:
the deck's 'unmodelled poly' diagnostic, which fires
on every Poly2 riser this block's two-layer channel
router draws (a poly shape touching Contact twice with
no resistor marker looks exactly like a drawn resistor
body to the deck) -- its SHAPE COUNT is in the pinned
substring, so the warning doubles as a regression test
on the router; and the pin-promotion notice on the two
block cells, whose per-bank labels all sit below the
top cell. This replaced a blanket 'any warning fails
the run', which a `klt` with better diagnostics turns
into a wall of red with nothing wrong in the layout.
lvs_cases     both point `klt lvs` at the SAME committed `netlist`
above; each pairs it against a different reference.
request     committed `klt lvs` request document under this
directory -- also directly runnable by hand (see its own
header comment for why both sides are pre-extracted/
hand-authored SPICE, not klt lvs's inline-extraction
shape).
reference   committed SPICE file under this directory, referenced by
`request`.
expect_status / expect_mismatch_count / expect_category_counts
the exact `klt lvs --format json` verdict. The 'match'
case is the positive control; the 'mismatch' case is the
negative control -- proof that a real seeded defect (not
an empty-vs-empty comparison) makes `klt lvs` fail loudly.
Keep in sync with gen_lvs_unit.py's own EXPECTED_* constants and the
two lvs_unit_ref_*.spice files' docstrings.
block_extractions / the block lvs_cases whose paths reach outside this
directory are issue #57's block-level layout (layout/adc-top/). They live
in this manifest, rather than in a second runner, so every LVS result this
repo has lands in one append-only record trail under the same assertions.
Two cases USED to expect `status: match` with a non-zero mismatch_count:
`comparator` and `adc_block`, each with two severity-`warning` findings of
ambiguous net pairing the comparer resolved structurally. Issue #116 found
those were not the load-resistor short they were attributed to -- they were
the comparator's differential INPUT, drawn on an internal net instead of the
cell's own `vinp`/`vinn` ports and written the same wrong way into the
reference, so LVS saw both sides agree and could only report the ambiguity.
Both are now 0 (`layout/adc-top/gen_comparator.py`, `prefer=` on
resolve_aliases). The load-resistor short is still real and still makes the
preamp's two OUTPUT nodes indistinguishable in the two cases that draw the
resistor bodies; `comparator_nores` (and, since #116, `adc_block_nores`) are
the companion cases that keep them distinct. See layout/adc-top/README.md
and layout/adc-top/parasitics/records/20260806-adc-block-comparator-input-open.md.

Issue #70 added the first CAPACITOR to any of these comparisons: `adc_cdac_cell` extracts a `cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield` and its reference states one. Issues #85 (the within-array per-weight interconnect) and #86 (its route out to the decode banks, the terminating unit's tie to `vcm`, and the top-plate mesh's tie to `topp`/`topn`) extended that to the tiled arrays: `adc_top`/`adc_block` now extract 1024 of them -- 512 real unit positions per side, 511 weighted plus DR-0011's terminating unit -- and their references state the same 1024. Note the shape of the reference: the LAYOUT draws `m` unit-size caps in parallel per weight, while `design/adc-top/adc_top.spice` models each weight as ONE lumped cap of the whole weight's area, so the reference is generated from the drawn unit list and not from the flattened schematic's cap devices. Each capacitance is the deck's area-only MiM value for the drawn plate (14.7316 fF), 14.6% below the PDK model card's area+fringe 17.245 fF for the same geometry -- a modelling difference reported in layout/lvs/records/, not absorbed by resizing the ratified plate. See layout/adc-top/README.md.

extract.name: lvs_unit
extract.role: single NMOS with Metal1 (34/10) pin labels S/D/G -- the layout side of both LVS cases below

lvs_cases.name: match
lvs_cases.role: positive control -- extracted lvs_unit vs. a hand-authored reference that matches it exactly

lvs_cases.name: mismatch
lvs_cases.role: negative control -- the SAME extracted lvs_unit vs. a reference with a deliberately seeded channel-width error (1.2um -> 2.4um). RE-BASELINED at the issue #70 pin bump: the seeded error is unchanged and still caught, but the pinned comparer now NAMES it (`device.property` on `w_um`, plus the four `as`/`ad`/`ps`/`pd` values that follow from a drawn width) instead of reporting only the collateral unmatched device/net pairs. 15 findings, 5 of them the actual defect -- a strictly sharper negative control than the 10 this expected before.

lvs_cases.name: adc_drv
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: local T-gate driver (`adc_drv`) -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: adc_tgate
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: CDAC bottom-plate decode T-gate -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: adc_tgate_dum
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: dummy-compensated input sampling switch (DR-0007/DR-0013) -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: adc_cdac_cell
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: one CDAC weighted-position cell, INCLUDING its unit MiM capacitor -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py). The reference's capacitance is the extraction deck's own area-only MiM model of the drawn plate (14.73 fF), not the PDK model card's area+fringe value for the same plate (17.24 fF); the 14.6% delta is a modelling difference no layout change could close and is reported in the LVS record, not absorbed here.

lvs_cases.name: adc_tp_sw
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: top-plate V_cm switch (adc_tp_sw, DR-0014) -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: comparator
lvs_cases.role: comparator cell WITH its load resistors (which extract as Poly2 shorts -- see the request document) -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py). RE-BASELINED at issue #116 from 2 accepted `topology` warnings to 0: those two rows were `$9`/`$4` (layout) paired ambiguously with `PREAMP_IN1`/`PREAMP_IN2` (reference) -- the signature of gen_comparator.py's missing `prefer=` on resolve_aliases(), which drew the preamp input pair on an INTERNAL net instead of the cell's own `vinp`/`vinn` ports and wrote the reference the same wrong way, so LVS could only see it as an ambiguity, not a break. With the ports carried through, both sides name the input pair's gates `vinp`/`vinn`, the ambiguity is gone, and pin_count rises 7 -> 9. See layout/adc-top/parasitics/records/20260806-adc-block-comparator-input-open.md.

lvs_cases.name: comparator_nores
lvs_cases.role: comparator cell WITHOUT the resistor bodies -- keeps pop/pon distinct -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: adc_top
lvs_cases.role: BLOCK: exactly what design/adc-top/adc_top.spice defines -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py) Since issues #85/#86 this comparison also covers the CDAC arrays' 1024 unit MiM capacitors -- 512 real positions per side, 511 weighted plus DR-0011's terminating unit -- wired to topp/topn on the top plate and to each weight's own decode node (XS<P|N>.X<w>.bp, or vcm for the terminating unit) on the bottom. The reference states the unit-size devices the LAYOUT draws, not the nine-per-side lumped per-weight devices adc_cdac_side writes; each capacitance is the extraction deck's area-only MiM value for the drawn 2.7136 um plate (14.7316 fF), 14.6% below the PDK model card's area+fringe 17.245 fF for the same geometry -- a modelling difference no layout change could close, reported here rather than absorbed by resizing the plate.

lvs_cases.name: adc_block
lvs_cases.role: BLOCK: the assembled block, adc_top plus the comparator -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py) Since issues #85/#86 this comparison also covers the CDAC arrays' 1024 unit MiM capacitors -- 512 real positions per side, 511 weighted plus DR-0011's terminating unit -- wired to topp/topn on the top plate and to each weight's own decode node (XS<P|N>.X<w>.bp, or vcm for the terminating unit) on the bottom. The reference states the unit-size devices the LAYOUT draws, not the nine-per-side lumped per-weight devices adc_cdac_side writes; each capacitance is the extraction deck's area-only MiM value for the drawn 2.7136 um plate (14.7316 fF), 14.6% below the PDK model card's area+fringe 17.245 fF for the same geometry -- a modelling difference no layout change could close, reported here rather than absorbed by resizing the plate. RE-BASELINED at issue #116 from 2 accepted `topology` warnings to 0: those two rows were `$167`/`$168` (layout) paired ambiguously with `XCMP.PREAMP_IN1`/`XCMP.PREAMP_IN2` (reference) -- both sides carrying the SAME defect, so the comparer could only call it ambiguous. The comparator's differential input is now genuinely on `topp`/`topn` (the CDAC top plates) in both, which is also why net_count drops 198 -> 196: the two dangling preamp-input nets no longer exist. See layout/adc-top/parasitics/records/20260806-adc-block-comparator-input-open.md.

lvs_cases.name: adc_block_nores
lvs_cases.role: SIMULATION COMPANION (issue #116), not a deliverable: the assembled block with the comparator's two 150 kohm p+ poly load-resistor BODIES omitted, so `pop`/`pon` survive extraction as distinct nets instead of collapsing onto `vdd`. This is the block-level analogue of `comparator_nores`, and it is what gives the post-layout comparator-inclusive core (layout/adc-top/parasitics/) a comparator that can actually make a decision -- with both preamp drains and both StrongARM latch input gates tied to `vdd` by the resistor short, the extracted ADC_BLOCK comparator has no gain and no decision, which is half of the stuck-code defect #116 root-caused. Expected fully clean: this case is what verifies the comparator's preamp-to-latch connectivity survives block assembly, which `adc_block` (resistors drawn) structurally cannot.
